headline: Iran rhetoric lifts Brent 1.4%; dollar at 19-month high sinks gold below $4,000; UST cash shut
summary: With the US cash bond market shut for Veterans Day, the dollar did the work: hike bets from Tuesday's hot CPI lifted the DXY to its highest since April 2025 and pushed spot gold below $4,000, while silver bounced about 1.5%. Oil rose off two-month lows as Iran said it will keep its enriched uranium and Gulf shipping attacks continued, but RBOB was flat. Bunds and OATs steadied after Tuesday's selloff, and Treasury futures pointed to yields 2–4bp higher for Thursday's reopen.
drivers: Dollar breakout on Fed hike bets

The DXY rose about 0.6% to near 102.9, its highest since April 2025, and dollar/yen neared 160 as markets fully priced a December hike with roughly a 10–12% chance of 50bp. Spot gold reversed an early rise to $4,067 and ended near $3,986; Comex Dec gold settled 0.7% lower at $4,000.50.
Iran hardline talk and Hormuz attacks lift crude

Iran's Rezaei said enriched nuclear material will not leave the country and threatened distant US bases if attacked. WTI rose 49¢ to $86.53 and Brent $1.27 to $92.76 after highs of $88.74 and $94.73, as 37 ship attacks in October showed Gulf risk is not gone.
OPEC+ supply back near pre-war levels

OPEC's report put October OPEC+ output at 41.23m bpd, up 2.04m bpd on the month and about 97% of February's level, with Saudi Arabia at 10.56m bpd from 8.37m. Demand forecasts were left unchanged, which capped the rally and kept RBOB flat at $2.6075.
Holiday-thin bonds: Europe steadies, US futures slip

The German 10-year eased about 2bp to 3.29% and the French 10-year about 5bp to 4.74%, taking the OAT-Bund spread to about 144bp, though a soft 2047/2056 Bund sale drew only €1.93bn of a €2.5bn target. US cash Treasuries were closed, but futures fell by the equivalent of 2–4bp in yield.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled +49¢ (+0.6%) at $86.53 after an $88.74 high; Brent +$1.27 at $92.76.
oil.why: Crude bounced from two-month lows after Iran's security chief Rezaei said enriched uranium will stay in the country and warned of strikes on distant US bases, which dented hopes of a quick deal. Shipping risk also stayed live, with 37 attacks in October, the most since the war began. Gains faded in the afternoon as OPEC data showed October OPEC+ output up 2.04m bpd to 41.23m bpd, near pre-war levels.
oil.outlook: Range of $83–90 with a mild downward bias as Saudi and Russian barrels return and CTAs have already cut longs to about 9%; $85 is first support. A tanker or pipeline strike that disrupts Hormuz flows would push WTI back above $90.
oil.watch: EIA stocks Thu Nov 12 (API showed a 9.8m bbl draw), the IEA report Fri Nov 13 and Iran headlines.

gas.note: Dec RBOB slipped 0.13¢ to $2.6075, a third lower settle and the lowest since Mar 4; ULSD +2.0% to $4.2113.
gas.why: Gasoline lagged the crude bounce: diesel led the complex on tight distillate supply, while RBOB eased as winter-grade blends and weak post-season demand weigh. It is down about 6% over three sessions and 21% this month. The AAA national average fell another 3¢ to $3.94, down 18¢ in a week and 41¢ in a month, though still 87¢ above a year ago.
gas.outlook: Bias lower in a $2.50–2.72 range while WTI stays under $90; pump prices should drift toward $3.85 by Thanksgiving. A crude rebound above $90 or a large gasoline draw would lift RBOB back toward $2.75.
gas.watch: EIA gasoline stocks and refinery runs Thu Nov 12 and the AAA daily average.

gold.note: Spot eased about 0.8% to near $3,986 after a $4,067 high; Comex Dec settled -0.7% at $4,000.50.
gold.why: An early bounce from Tuesday's near-3% drop faded as the dollar index climbed to its highest since April 2025 near 102.9, making bullion dearer for non-US buyers. Markets now fully price a December Fed hike, see about a 10–12% chance of 50bp, and price close to 75bp of hikes by next September, which raises the cost of holding non-yielding gold. Central-bank buying is still giving the market a floor.
gold.outlook: Bias lower in a $3,900–4,080 range while the dollar breaks out; a daily close below $3,950 would open the late-October low near $3,886. A soft PPI or a dollar pullback would bring $4,050–4,100 back.
gold.watch: US PPI Fri Nov 13, Treasury reopen Thu Nov 12, Fed speakers and the dollar.

silver.note: Comex Dec settled +1.5% at $52.00; spot near $51.8 after an early run to about $53.5.
silver.why: Silver outperformed gold as bargain hunters and short-covering returned after Tuesday's near-3% fall, helped by firmer copper and palladium and a record close for European stocks. It hit about $53.5 in London trade, then gave back much of the gain as the dollar rose to a 19-month high. The gold/silver ratio eased to about 77 from 79.
silver.outlook: Range of $50–54 with a neutral bias: industrial demand and a falling ratio help, but rising real yields cap rallies. A close above $53.6 would target $55, while a break of $50 would retest the October low.
silver.watch: US PPI Nov 13, chip stocks, copper and the dollar.

us2y.note: Cash market closed for Veterans Day; Tuesday close near 4.73–4.75%, futures implied a few bp higher.
us2y.why: No cash trading took place, but Treasury futures fell by the equivalent of about 2–4bp in yield as Tuesday's hike repricing settled in. Fed funds futures fully price a 25bp December hike, with about a 10–12% chance of 50bp and better-than-even odds of another in January, after Waller's call to consider 50bp and Logan's push for at least two more hikes.
us2y.outlook: Bias higher in a 4.68–4.85% range while officials push for hikes; firm PPI and more 50bp talk would target 4.85%. A soft PPI or Fed leaders pushing back on a bigger move would pull it toward 4.65%.
us2y.watch: Cash reopen and jobless claims Thu Nov 12, PPI Fri Nov 13 and the Dec 8–9 FOMC.

us5y.note: Closed for the holiday; Tuesday close near 4.83%, with futures pointing modestly higher.
us5y.why: The 5-year sits where a longer hiking cycle bites hardest, and futures trade on Wednesday suggested a further 2–4bp rise on Thursday's reopen. Markets now see close to 75bp of Fed hikes by next September, and the dollar's jump to a 19-month high showed global investors still buying that story while cash bonds were shut.
us5y.outlook: Range of 4.75–4.95% with an upward bias while hike pricing builds; a soft PPI would bring 4.75%, while a firm one and 50bp talk would open 4.95%.
us5y.watch: Thursday reopen, PPI Fri Nov 13 and Fed speakers.

us10y.note: Closed for Veterans Day; Tuesday close near 5.00%, and futures suggested a retest of 5.01%+ on Thursday.
us10y.why: With cash bonds shut, futures fell by the equivalent of 2–4bp in yield, pointing to the 10-year revisiting Tuesday's highs above 5.01% when trading resumes. Tuesday's 10-year auction was the first since 2006 to set a fixed coupon of 5% or more, and soft demand there plus a hike fully priced for December keep supply concerns in focus ahead of the 30-year sale.
us10y.outlook: Range of 4.92–5.12% with an upward bias while hike pricing builds; above 5.12% opens October's highs near 5.3%. A soft PPI would bring 4.92%.
us10y.watch: Reopen and the 30-year auction Thu Nov 12, PPI Fri Nov 13.

us30y.note: No cash trading; Tuesday close near 5.36%, with bond futures lower ahead of the 30-year sale.
us30y.why: The long end was closed, but bond futures slipped with the rest of the curve as dealers prepared for Thursday's 30-year auction after Tuesday's 10-year sale left them with about 9.7%, the most since May. The curve has been bear-flattening because faster hikes are seen capping long-run inflation, so the 30-year has risen less than the 2-year.
us30y.outlook: Range of 5.28–5.45% with a mild upward bias; a weak 30-year auction could push it to 5.45%, while a strong one and a soft PPI would bring it back to 5.28%.
us30y.watch: 30-year auction Thu Nov 12, PPI Fri Nov 13.

de2y.note: About flat to 1bp lower near 3.07% (Reuters) after Tuesday's 8bp jump to a near two-week high.
de2y.why: The front end held most of Tuesday's rise because traders nudged up bets on a December ECB hike to near certainty after Lane said a hike would be prudent if the data hold and Nagel called it rather obvious. With US cash bonds closed there was no fresh US lead, so the 2-year mostly consolidated.
de2y.outlook: Range of 3.00–3.15% with a slight upward bias while a December hike to 2.75% is priced; a lasting oil slide that pulls inflation expectations lower is the main downside trigger.
de2y.watch: Euro-area GDP Fri Nov 13, ECB speakers and the Dec 17 meeting.

de5y.note: Down about 2–3bp to near 3.13% as Bunds steadied after Tuesday's spillover from Treasuries.
de5y.why: Belly Bunds recovered part of Tuesday's US-driven selloff in thin holiday trade as the market calmed. Brent still near its lowest since late August limits the inflation worry for Europe, even as ECB officials line up behind a third hike this year. Euro weakness against a 19-month-high dollar was another reason for steadiness.
de5y.outlook: Range of 3.05–3.20% with a neutral bias; a 10-year Treasury above 5.10% would lift it to 3.20%, while softer euro-area data would bring 3.05%.
de5y.watch: Euro-area GDP Fri Nov 13 and the Treasury reopen Thu.

de10y.note: Down about 2bp to near 3.29–3.30% after a 4bp rise Tuesday.
de10y.why: The benchmark eased as markets calmed after the hot US CPI, helped by Brent near two-month lows and no US cash trading to extend the selloff. Germany's long-bond sale was soft, raising €1.93bn of a €2.5bn target with a 1.3x cover on the 2056, which kept the long end from rallying and the curve steeper.
de10y.outlook: Range of 3.22–3.36% with a slight upward bias while US yields climb; a 10-year Treasury above 5.10% or hawkish ECB news would push it above 3.36%.
de10y.watch: Treasury reopen Thu Nov 12, euro-area GDP and Fitch's Germany review Fri Nov 13.

de30y.note: About 1bp higher near 3.68%; a soft long Bund sale undercut the long end.
de30y.why: Germany sold only €1.93bn of a €2.5bn target across its 2047 and 2056 Bunds, with the 2056 just 1.3 times covered and 28% retained, so the long end lagged while shorter Bunds rallied. Heavy German issuance for defence and infrastructure keeps term premium rising, and the 10s30s curve steepened by about 3bp.
de30y.outlook: Range of 3.62–3.75% with a mild upward bias on supply; a break above 3.75% would need a weak US 30-year auction or another soft German sale.
de30y.watch: US 30-year auction Thu Nov 12 and next week's German supply.

fr2y.note: Little changed to slightly higher near 3.65%, anchored by near-certain ECB December hike pricing.
fr2y.why: Short OATs track ECB expectations rather than French fiscal risk, so they held Tuesday's rise as Lane and Nagel kept a December hike close to fully priced. Lower oil and calmer markets helped longer OATs more than the front end, so the curve flattened from the front.
fr2y.outlook: Range of 3.55–3.72% with a slight upward bias while ECB hike pricing firms; a lasting oil drop that cools inflation is the main downside trigger.
fr2y.watch: French final CPI Fri Nov 13, ECB speakers and the ECB Dec 17.

fr5y.note: About flat near 4.22%, holding Tuesday's rise while the long end rallied.
fr5y.why: Middle-maturity OATs are caught between near-certain ECB hike pricing and the narrowing French risk premium, and the two offset on Wednesday. The spread to Germany at this tenor narrowed slightly as energy prices stayed lower and political risk did not flare, while thin holiday trade limited follow-through.
fr5y.outlook: Range of 4.12–4.30% with a neutral bias; budget progress would pull it toward 4.12%, while a government crisis or hawkish ECB surprise would lift it toward 4.30%.
fr5y.watch: French final CPI Nov 13 and the Senate budget debate.

fr10y.note: Down about 5bp to near 4.74% (Reuters benchmark); spread to Bunds near 144bp from 178bp in October.
fr10y.why: OATs outperformed as markets calmed after the US CPI jolt and Brent stayed near its lowest since late August, cutting deficit and inflation worries for higher-debt borrowers. The OAT-Bund spread narrowed about 3bp to 144bp, versus a 2011-high 178bp in October, even as French politics and talk of Lagarde's early exit keep a risk premium in place.
fr10y.outlook: Range of 4.65–4.85% with the spread held near 138–155bp; a budget passed even by decree could tighten it toward 138bp, while a government crisis would push it above 160bp.
fr10y.watch: French final CPI Nov 13, the Senate budget debate and the Dec 9 Senate vote.

fr30y.note: Down about 2bp to near 5.31%, with the long end leading OAT gains.
fr30y.why: The longest OATs gained most as lower oil eased long-run inflation fears and investors added back French duration after the spread retreated from October's highs. That came despite a soft German long-bond sale the same day, showing demand for spread over Bunds rather than for duration in general.
fr30y.outlook: Range of 5.22–5.40% with a neutral bias; a credible budget path could take it toward 5.22%, while a political setback or weak US 30-year auction would lift it toward 5.40%.
fr30y.watch: Senate budget debate, US 30-year auction Thu Nov 12 and rating reviews.

watch: Next: US cash Treasuries reopen with jobless claims, EIA stocks and the 30-year auction Thu Nov 12; US PPI, euro-area GDP, French CPI and the IEA report Fri Nov 13; then the Fed Dec 8–9 and ECB Dec 17.
